asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795846532
asks.decision: whether the first move is a live walk of what is built
asks.text: Most of Direct Sun is built. Before more design, a walk of two saves that already exist: DIRECT_SUN_TUNING_SITTING_20261126_DASHERS (rows of colonists in open, roof, tent, parasol and a wall's lee, with animals dashing shade to shade) and CROWN_SHADOW_GREATBOLE_REVIEW on ArchSmall (32 greatboles with drawn crown shadows at a sun of 15 degrees). It shows what we would otherwise ask you to predict: whether shade reads at a glance (T3), whether the drawn crown shadow stays, and how a wall's short lee looks beside where a mountain's long one would fall.

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795846532
asks.decision: what makes one mountain throw a longer shadow than another
asks.text: Picture a lone ridge rising from flat sand and a cliff that is the edge of a wide massif, at the same sun. Do they throw the same band of shade, or does the bigger mass throw a longer one? And a small rock outcrop with no roof over it (the game clears any natural roof patch under 20 cells): is that a mountain that casts, or a rock?
asks.evidence_against: The game keeps a coarse height: rock where the generator's elevation passed 0.70, thin rock roof above 0.728, thick rock roof above 0.798 (GenStep_RocksFromGrid). So the obvious answer, height from the roof band, makes a massif's deep core throw farther than its edge; but his words 'mountain-covered squares' would leave an unroofed outcrop casting only a wall's lee.

asks.author: rm-role-designer-1795846532
asks.decision: whether the mountain's long shadow is drawn on the ground
asks.text: How does the player feel the mountain: by a dark band drawn on the ground down-sun, or by the shade overlay and the cell readout only?
asks.evidence_against: Vanilla draws a rock's shadow at height 1, so with no drawn band the player sees a short shadow beside a long band of felt relief (what you see is not what they feel). His ruling on the greatbole's drawn crown shadow, due by 2026-12-04, is the same kind of work and may settle this one.

failure_modes: What you see is not what they feel: the mountain's long shade and the crowns' shade are felt by pawns, but vanilla draws a rock's shadow at height 1, so he sees a short shadow beside a long band of relief, and invisible shade reads as a bug rather than as the mountain on the map.

Shade floods the map: at a low fixed sun (the Long Shade clamps 2 to 30 degrees) a cast of height x cot E reaches about 11 cells per unit height at 5 degrees, so a mountain or a forest can shade most open ground and the sun stops being a thing he plans around, the opposite of 'a feel for said mountain depending on the sun angle'.

Built but undecidable: Direct Sun has no folder of its own (code in Creature Behaviors, defs in Environmental Hazards and three biome mods inside mandrake.rm.biomes) and many built parts have no proof row (moving shade, haze, sun pathing, standing casters), so bars cannot be decided by the pipeline and a change in a neighbour breaks the sun silently.
